seoTitle: SRT Subtitle Timing Shifter and Drift Fixer
metaDescription: Delay or advance SRT subtitles by an offset, or stretch them with two reference points to fix drift from frame rate mismatch. Private, text only.
intro: Shifts every subtitle cue by a fixed number of seconds, or rescales all times with two reference points to fix gradual drift.
why:
Subtitles that start in sync but drift later usually come from a frame rate mismatch, for example 23.976 against 25 fps. Two reference points give a straight line: new time equals a times old time plus b. The tool solves that line and applies it to every cue.

For a constant delay use the offset mode. Cues that would end before zero are dropped. The converter on this site shifts by milliseconds too, but has no stretch mode.
howTo: Pick Shift for a constant delay, or Stretch for drift.
For Stretch, enter two times where the subtitle is now and when it should be.

faq.q: How do I pick the reference points?
faq.a: Choose the first and the last line of dialogue. Note when each is heard in the video and its current cue time.
Seconds, m:ss or h:mm:ss, with decimals.
No. Only the times. Cues are renumbered.
